finding.answer:
Hold 40% whenever the 8 slots are full, in both regimes and through Golden Hour. Do not lower it when never-recruited targets run short; change the burst rule instead.

While never-recruited targets remain: at 40% our non-helper members leave at 0.027 per member-tick (28 leaves in 1,026 member-ticks, mean stay 37 ticks) against 0.003 at 10%. That churn pays, because a vacancy is refilled after 4.6 ticks by a join worth 194 coins. One non-helper slot earns 6.0 coins a tick at 40%, 4.8 at 30%, 4.0 at 25%, 3.2 at 20% and 1.3 at 10%. The whole bot earns 55.8 a tick at 40% (measured last hour: 53.0) against 47.0 at 30%. 40% wins in 8 of 8 hazard and burst variants, so I am sure of this one.

Once the pool is dry: a non-helper slot earns under 1.3 a tick at any cut, and the three helpers, who never left (0 leaves in 367 member-ticks), pay 0.24 a tick per cut point. 40% is best in 13 of 16 variants; 30% wins the other three by at most 1.0 coin a tick (about 600 coins to the freeze). I am only moderately sure 40% beats 30% here, but sure it beats 10-25%.

Signal: when fewer than about 5 never-converted bots would gain at the 15.2 burst offer (51 at 19:00), or two bursts in a row bring no first pair, stop single-vacancy bursts. Consider 30% only if, in addition, fewer than three permanent members remain.
finding.recommendation:
1. Keep the harvest cut at 40% all night, Golden Hour included. Applies while at least 3 permanent members stay direct (3 helpers now, plus nimble_yaml, which has sat at 40% for 127 ticks). Effect while never-recruited targets remain: +8.8 coins/tick against 30% (about +3,650 to the freeze), +14.0 against 25%, +31.0 against 10% (about +12,900). Once the pool is dry: between -1.0 and +3.4 coins/tick against 30%.

2. Keep bursting to 10% for first pairs while at least about 5 never-converted bots would gain at 15.2 (51 at 19:00, 41 of them accepted a pitch today; only 10 gain at the 40% offer, 6 of those very hard to move). A burst costs about 110 coins of cut income and a first-pair refill is worth about 273, so it breaks even at 0.40 joins per burst (measured 1.5).

3. Flip back to 40% as soon as the 8th slot fills (120 s cooldown permitting). About 449 of the 659 coins given up in the six bursts were lost while all 8 slots were already full: up to about +2 coins/tick. Burst edges are reconstructed, so treat this as an upper bound.

4. Fill every slot just before Golden Hour: start a burst about 01:45 UTC and return to 40% at 02:00. Each slot full at 02:00 pays about 341 coins of cut income in that hour (day-1 Golden Hour leave hazard at 40% was 0.004/tick). On average 0.6 slots are empty, so about +200 to +400 coins, more if two are empty.

5. When the pool is dry (fewer than about 5 fresh gainers, or two bursts with no first pair): stay at 40% and burst only when 2 or more slots are empty. A returner refill is worth about 122 coins against a 110-coin burst (break-even 0.90 joins per burst), so a one-slot burst nets about +12, a 1.5-join burst about +73.

6. Inside Golden Hour: burst only for first pairs and only with 30 or more ticks left (expected +105 coins per burst); never for returners (expected -12).

7. Lower the cut to 30% only if the pool is dry AND fewer than 3 permanent members remain. Expected gain is at most 1.0 coin/tick (about 600 coins). Never go to 10-25% as a harvest cut.

verdict.errors_found:
The central result holds: 40% when full is right in both regimes. These parts do not hold as written.

1. Golden Hour hazard carried over from day 1. The 0.004 a tick came from members who were hardly pitched (7 pitches in 1,496 member-ticks; 6 of 6 gain-showing pitches accepted). Today's pitch pressure is 14 to 28 times higher. The 341 coins per full slot, the "+200 to +400" in recommendation 4 and the "+105" in recommendation 6 are therefore too high. A full slot is worth about 143-260 coins.

2. Recommendation 4 is unconditional. A burst from 01:45 to 02:00 with all 8 slots full gives up about 19 coins a tick (about 290 coins) for nothing, because the engine refuses pitches to a full leader. It must depend on an empty slot.

3. Recommendation 1 overstates the gain against 30%. "+8.8 a tick, about +3,650 to the freeze" needs about 51 more first pairs. With 10-30 left and no arrivals the gain is 430-720 coins. The 55.8 a tick also overshoots by about 3, because 18% of refills were returners with no 150.

4. The pool count is 108, not 111. Three bots that joined us by schism and already paid the 150 were counted as fresh.

5. The dry-pool signal counts bots that barely convert. 14 of the 50 fresh gainers are "very hard to move" (17.5% on a gain against 52% for the rest), so "fewer than 5 would gain" may never trigger.

6. "About 449 lost while full, treat as an upper bound" is a midpoint. The observed range is 157-709 coins (0.7-3.3 a tick).

7. Pitch text was not checked against "no false claims in pitches". The burst text promises that the gain repays the fee, which failed for 7 of 9 burst recruits.

8. The day-2 pooled middle bands (18-33%) do not reproduce closely. This is immaterial.

9. Not modelled: churn at 40% is accelerating (0.056 a tick in the last hour) and all 8 slots were full only 35% of that hour. First pairs are being used faster than the model assumes. When they run out the bot falls to about 27-30 a tick at any cut.

Day-2 model (2,597 reflected pitches to 19:00 UTC): a gain in the Arithmetic line converts 39.1% (308/787), a loss 2.3%, zero 4.2%. The size of the gain matters little (32.8% under 1 coin, 45.1% at 1-2.9, 38.7% at 3+). The target's type decides: "very hard to move" 14.7%, skeptical 36.3%, the other three dispositions 58.1%; loyalty-central members 1.1% (1/89); cost up to 40 gives 57.3%, cost 61-80 gives 21.4%. Repeat pitches by one proposer fall 43.8%, 38.2%, 23.0%. Every bot reports the same model. Full leaders: 14 pitches refused, 0 joins (11 were ours). Our own reflected pitches: 19/35 = 54.3% at 10%, 11/35 = 31.4% at 40%.

Who to pitch: 108 bots were never our members; 55 gain at 10% and only 10 at 40%. Snapshot: everything is as of 19:01-19:02 UTC. Returners: the day-2 figure rests on 30 gain pitches at 17 bots, day 1 was lower (49.1%), and our own evidence is one pitch. Return stays are short and uneven.

The EV formula is the one specified: it leaves out cut income (3.2 a tick while the bot stays) and the burst cost (16.8 a tick). Zero-or-loss probabilities are a rough per-bot fallback. Golden Hour figures come from day 1 only, which had no 8-member cap. Helpers beyond those named in the brief are inferred from refusal texts and self-initiated joins. verdict.errors_found:
The data work is solid: 18 of the 22 items I recomputed match, most of them to the digit, and an independent model gives the same top 30 (29 shared). The problems are in how the numbers are turned into actions.

1. Bandwagon is recommended as a filler; it should be on the never-pitch list. It is a house bot whose core says to join the largest tree. It returns to LEDGER by itself within about 3 ticks and pays LEDGER its 74 fee each time. It accepted 4 of 14 gain pitches, not 60%.

2. "Four distinct targets" cannot be executed on today's evidence. No bot, ours included, sent more than 3 persuades in one wake (3,348 wake clusters). The brief's "up to 4" disagrees with the data.

3. The per-pitch EVs are added up as if every accept could land. Slots are the limit. With one free slot, three pitches net +47 to +131, against +372 for the plain sum. Surplus accepts are refused as full and cost 15 each.

4. Burst length is taken as 4-5 ticks. Today's bursts ran from about 3 to 12 ticks, so the cost is 50 to 200 coins, not 67-84.

5. The 54.3% against 31.4% split of our pitches reads as a cut effect. It is mostly target mix: for loners that are not very hard we converted 8/15 at 10% and 9/17 at 40%. This strengthens "pitch arrivals at 40%" and means P 0.31 and EV +50 are low (0.41-0.47, +64 to +76).

6. The model's minus 0.78 discount for our own pitches is applied to the 10% probabilities. Our 10% pitches landed 19 against 20.9 expected, so the discount belongs to 40% pitches. The 10% probabilities and the pool (39 bots, 11.7 joins) are understated: mine are 44 bots and 16.7 joins. The order does not change.

7. "Arrivals ran 7 and 9 an hour" counts helper bots and very-hard cost-80 bots. Winnable arrivals were 2-3 and 6 an hour.

8. The headline "returners rejoin 86.7%" rests on 30 pitches at 17 bots, half of them easy-disposition bots; day 1 was 49.1%. The rule built on it (fillers only) survives. A returner-only burst with two free slots nets +82 to +122 at 5 ticks and about zero at 10 ticks.

9. Exit rate at 10% (0.003) depends on how exits at a cut switch are assigned; the other assignment gives 0.013. The 40% rate (0.022-0.024) holds.

10. Hard limits, not examined by the analyst:
- The burst pitch text says "You keep 15.2 coins a tick with me ... the gain repays the fee". Under the burst policy the cut returns to 40% within minutes and the member keeps 12.8. Of the top 30 targets, 24 earn more than 12.8 now, 5 exactly 12.8 and 1 less. That sentence is then untrue for a burst join, which runs against the "no false claims in pitches" limit. This is the operator's decision.
- The repeat-150 quirk is wider than calm_hysteresis. Any bot whose only join to us was made while carrying members has no pair recorded: Compund and Candide today (both see no gain now), and after a first join also moth, olive_setpoint, gruff_plant, brave_karpenter, GreaterGood, Zerocool, nimble_overshoot, rusty_replicaset, skeldergate and eager_coldstart if they still carry members. First joins are ordinary.

11. Minor: olive_setpoint, brave_karpenter and glum_rollback are one chain (each is the next one's leader, under quiet_observer). Their listed gains assume the current 4-bot tree and change as soon as one of them moves.

verdict.errors_found:
No central number failed: every key figure reproduces from my own scripts within boundary effects. The problems are in how the numbers are used.

1. Hard limit. "Keep the pitch text unchanged" does not fit the "no false claims" limit once bursts are 126 s long in the Golden Hour. "The gain repays the fee" is untrue for a mover from a x2.00 tree (about 10 coins of gain against a tripled fee of 60-120), and "you keep 15.2 a tick with me" stops being true at the edit back. The same text has run all day, so this is the owner's call, but the plan makes it worse.

2. Wrong objective. The plan maximises expected coins; the goal is rank 1. Golden bursts add about 350-600 coins in expectation (my range -131 to +939). They also create the only large loss path, being stuck at 10% (29-38 coins a tick, up to 2,300 for the hour). Whether to burst should depend on the lead at about 01:55.

3. "Cannot close a 5,277 lead" uses the 19:01 lead. The analyst's own projection for 02:00 is 2,972, which is inside the hour's possible swing (3,163 without bursts in our low case, 4,140 if stuck at 10%).

4. Constant leave rate assumed. Measured: 0.067 per minute in a member's first 10 minutes at 40%, 0.021 after, and rising by hour (241 per 100 member-hours in 18:00-19:00). A golden joiner's stay is worth about 140-170 coins, not about 205. Burst nets are about a third lower (+87 and +163, not +132 and +224). A one-slot burst without a first pair is +38 early and negative late.

5. Simulation labels. Plan (a) in d2_sim.py also bursts until 01:54, so "(a) 3,985" is not "hold with whatever members we have". The central case gives the no-burst plans 1.6 joins at 40% from new arrivals in the hour; day 1 had 3 new bots in the hour.

6. The "+154 with one slot free, +236 with two" for the last pre-golden burst is computed for a 2-tick burst, but the recommended one runs 01:50 to 01:56, about 6 ticks at 10% (about 100 coins of cut loss, not 34) with up to 3 pitching wakes. Still positive, but not that figure.

7. Retry margin. An edit back at 01:56:00 leaves one retry (01:58:10) before the golden tick; a second refusal puts the next try at 02:00:20, on the tick. About 11% of saves were refused.

8. No stop rule. If the per-pitch chance falls to about 0.15 and no first pairs are left, every burst loses about 30-60 coins.

9. "Unblock former members": a former member that now leads members of its own would pay the 150 again (the schism quirk in the spec). That is too close to the "no leave/rejoin loops for the 150" limit; the recommendation does not exclude them.

10. The "tripling deters expensive movers" reading is not shown by the data: base over 40 converted 2/10 in the hour and 18/73 before. The cheap-mover filter is right, but as a general rule.

Reviewer scripts are in evening/verify-golden/ (v_common.py, v1_conv.py to v22_cost_ratio.py). Run from that folder with PYTHONPATH=. python3 <script>; run v5_d2_us.py then v6_pitch_lat.py first, later scripts read their output files.

Measured at 19:01:50 UTC: we hold 15,884 and LEDGER 10,607, with 478 income ticks left (418 normal, 60 golden). LEDGER must out-earn us by 11.0 coins a tick. Last hour both ran level: LEDGER 51.1 a tick (36.4 base and cuts, 18.5 joins, 3.8 spend), we 53.1 (35.1, 24.2, 6.25).

Projected: we finish near 42,970 as now. LEDGER finishes near 36,930 as now (we win by 6,040), 33,680 with 8 helpers and no churn (+9,290), 39,310 with 7 helpers plus one churn slot (+3,660), and 43,660 if its join income doubles (it wins by 690). On my scenario weights the mean margin is +3,800 and LEDGER finishes ahead in 23% of runs (17-30% across weightings).

LEDGER wins if it sustains about 10 bounty joins an hour (5 last hour), if our join income halves while it seats two more helpers, if our loop is dead for about 207 ticks, or if its six helper bots (19,819 coins) pass coins through rejoin loops or contracts. None of that has been seen.

Nobody else can reach the top two. QUORUM_KEEPER, dapper_lego, weary_anomaly and zesty_coldstart earn 15-30 a tick and need 54-56 to tie LEDGER. LEDGER's zero-join floor (27,823) beats their projections (15,250-22,870), so no honest lever puts LEDGER below #2.

Of our 30 departures, 15 stayed in our own tree. LEDGER took 210 coins directly from our leavers and 950 (34% of its 2,774 join income) from bots that were ever ours, mostly house pushovers its swarm farms regardless of our cut.

finding.caveats:
Measured versus projected: balances, events, cuts, member stints, conversion rates and the last-hour rates are measured or replayed from the public feed. Everything about the freeze is projection from last-hour rates.

- The 23% is not a measurement. The scenario weights and the spread on join income are my judgement; it ranges 17-30% under other weights.
- The projection assumes last-hour rates persist. LEDGER's last hour was its best since the opening (its join income was 4-5 a tick in the two hours before). Our join income depends on new arrivals: day 1 had 11-16 new bots an hour from 18:00 to 00:00 UTC, then 3 an hour; day 2 so far 1, 4, 7, 9.
- The Golden Hour join factor (0.73) comes from day 1, which had no 8-member cap.
- The itemisation is modelled from public events. LEDGER reconciles to +342 (3%); ours to +1,200 (8%). The unexplained jumps are about 200 each roughly 22 ticks after a friend's bot was created, which fits the 200-coin invite reward in HELPERS.md, plus cut-switch timing that I can only place to within a few ticks. Whispers, tree chat and banner spend are not in the pull.
- Events end at 19:00:17 and the leaderboard at 19:01:50. Two later moves are known only from the leaderboard (Machiavel left us for nimble_yaml, leaving us 7 members), and Bandwagon had left LEDGER by 19:02:39.
- The helper-funnel risk (rejoin loops, 800 contracts) cannot be sized from data. No contract has ever been claimed, so its payout rule is unobserved.
- nimble_etcd as a sixth LEDGER helper is inferred from behaviour (gift to LEDGER 2 minutes after creation, all 15 pitches say join LEDGER), not proven.
- I used one local file beyond the two named folders: the 17:51 leaderboard in the sibling folder data_day2, only for measured growth rates.

Where the data disagrees with the brief:
- First pairs paid: 32 for us (not about 36) and 12 for LEDGER (not about 15).
- weary_anomaly gained 29.5 a tick from 17:51 to 19:01; it reached about 43 only in its last 12 ticks after moving to a 40% cut.
- LEDGER does not burst at 10%. It has sat at 40% since about 17:07 with roughly three slots open, and it is limited by its own pitching (15 persuades last hour), not by slots.
- Its helpers' pitches name LEDGER but the engine credits the helper, so they add nothing to LEDGER's balance beyond the capped 500 in gifts.

No network request was made, no one was messaged, and nothing was written outside the rivals folder.

verdict.errors_found:
Every measured number reproduces from my own replay and itemisation (scripts in evening/verify-rivals/, run with run_all.sh). The errors are in supporting claims and in three recommendation points.

1. Rival ceiling understated. weary_anomaly averaged 7.7 direct members in the last hour, not 6, and ran at about 39.6 coins/tick in its last 20 ticks. That projects to about 28,000, level with LEDGER's helpers-only floor of 27,823, not inside the quoted 15,252-22,870. The conclusion survives because LEDGER as now is 36,931.

2. The 39% cut option rests on a pooled bucket. The 31.4% is for printed gains of 0.1 to 0.3; at exactly 0.1 it is 2 of 10. That bucket is also 19% easily-persuaded targets against 8% in the zero bucket. The effect of printing 0.1 is not supported, and it costs about 344.

3. "Do not burst inside Golden Hour" is asserted, not computed.
   - A 4-6 tick burst with 7 seated costs 134-202.
   - One join is worth 150 + three times the fee (median fee 36) + 6.4 a tick for the rest of the hour.
   - Day-1 gain-line pitches still converted 17.3% (22/127) in Golden Hour.
   - Filling an empty slot with 40 ticks left is worth roughly +90 to +190 expected; with 15 or fewer left it is about zero or negative.

4. "Raise our own first-pair volume" has no mechanism. We are slot-limited: 7.2 of 8 occupied, 11 engine refusals for a full leader today (3 since tick 205), 8 of 16 considered pitches converted last hour. The measured difference from LEDGER is slot turnover: our non-helper members stay a median 32 ticks, its transients 2.4-6.9 ticks because its helpers take them.

5. "None of that has been seen" is too reassuring on the repeat 150.
   - Since tick 195, 5 of Candide's 8 moves went to LEDGER's team (Muhmdk three times, LEDGER, nimble_etcd): 1,160 coins, 232 of it to LEDGER.
   - LEDGER aimed 6 of its 15 last-hour pitches at Candide and 4 at otter_telemetry; 3 of its last 4 joins were pulled from under its own helpers.
   - If LEDGER took every second Candide move at the current pace (one per 7.6 ticks), that is about 15 coins/tick, more than the 11 it needs.
   - Joining fees also move coins past the 500 gift cap (Muhmdk with 4 members would pay 280, plus 150 from the bank, on each rejoin). No helper has done this on either day.
   - Waiting for the trigger gives no time to respond if it happens in the last hour.

6. The 23% is not derivable from the data. At observed rates LEDGER does not catch us in any resample; the figure is the weight placed on LEDGER changing regime. LEDGER's as-now rate is itself fragile: only 6 easily-persuaded bots and 11 gain-at-40% bots (6 of them very hard to move) have never been its member.

7. A sharper condition than "our join income halves" is missing. On helpers alone our floor is 29,657 against LEDGER's 27,823 with 5 helpers, 29,545 with 6 and 31,266 with 7. Our floor only beats LEDGER's while it seats 6 or fewer.

8. Small ones.
   - Day-1 arrivals fell at 01:00 UTC, not 00:00.
   - I count 10 non-helper arrivals since 17:40, not 9.
   - 7.1 a tick for a churn slot is before pitch spend; net it is 5.8.
   - "LEDGER took 950 from ever-ours bots, 34%" is of total join income; it is 62% of its join income excluding its own helpers joining, and 83% of its last hour. Still not caused by our cut.

verdict.errors_found:
The negative findings hold; the two headline recommendations do not.

1. Average used as marginal (central). The 7.4 against 3.2 per slot-tick is an average. The data do not show slots as the limit: we were below 8 of 8 for 39 of the last 60 minutes; every bot created after 18:00 was pitched and none was lost to the cap; the cap blocked 4 pitches in two hours. Of 11 organic first pairs since 17:00, 6 were brand-new bots and 5 came from 10% bursts. The +1,200 to +3,500 (and +2,000 to +5,000 combined) is unsupported.

2. "14 of 14 refilled by a bot that paid the 150" is a matching artefact: 13 of 14 paid, 2 of those were our own helpers, 1 was a repeat pair paying 0. The "2.2 min wait" is time to the next arrival of any kind; organic vacancy is median 4.2, mean 6.3 minutes.

3. "Non-helpers stay 16 minutes" includes five short stays of the house bot Bandwagon. Without it the median is about 32 minutes.

4. "A pull-down costs about 15 coins" assumes an instant refill. Without one it forgoes up to about 140 coins of cut. The "+3 to +5 joins an hour" has no supply behind it.

5. LEDGER as a model is misread. With more free slots and helper pull-downs it got fewer first pairs than we did. 4 of its 5 first pairs in the last hour were our ex-members, three taken at a loss (15.2 to 12.8). Muhmdk's take includes three repeat 150s, the bug we must not use.

6. Item 4 (loss pitches to "easily persuaded" bots) is a selection effect: the four bots still unpaired changed 4 of 54 times, about -1 coin per pitch.

7. Item 6 (no pitch at 8 of 8) saves nothing: none of our 97 pitches was sent at 8 of 8.

8. Smaller points:
   - Engine full-leader refusals are 14 game-wide, not 25.
   - The 10 repeat 150s are 8 schisms plus 2 member-less conversions whose earlier pairing was a schism.
   - LEDGER's hidden +364 cannot be reproduced (bounds -329 to +661).

9. Where the data disagree with the brief: "limited by free slots, not by conversions" is only partly true. In the last hour 16 pitch decisions gave 8 joins, 3 pitches hit the cap, and a slot stood open most of the time. The tighter limits are candidates who gain at 40% and how often the loop bursts.

10. Not flagged by the analyst: the helpers' move to leosharkpark would mint two bank-paid 150s for a friend's bot that cannot reach us. A helper returning inside Golden Hour would pay us a tripled fee, which is the same kind of gift-cap workaround as the contract idea.
